energy_accounting.study_energy_disclosure: Built-in Linux chip energy counters across 300 builds; no wall power meter used.

claims.statement: Real compilers break any single descriptive law, so this study establishes a seven-part yardstick to measure them.
Maximum compiler optimization burns upfront chip energy that never pays back on up to thirty percent of programs.
Fingerprinting code by variable position reuses compiled builds safely, cutting warm Rust compile energy over four hundred times.
Headline outcome: 448.5x Rebuild Energy Cut · 0/500 Mix-Ups (Built-in Linux chip energy counters across 300 builds; no wall power meter used.)

easy_read.easy_title: When Heavy Code Optimization Wastes Power
three_points_one_idea_sentences: This study is about when heavy code optimization wastes power.
Real compilers break any single descriptive law, so this study establishes a seven-part yardstick to measure them.
Maximum compiler optimization burns upfront chip energy that never pays back on up to thirty percent of programs.
Fingerprinting code by variable position reuses compiled builds safely, cutting warm Rust compile energy over four hundred times.
Key result: 448.5x Rebuild Energy Cut · 0/500 Mix-Ups.
Built-in computer chip counters recorded the energy used.
